Depends on a default fetcher configured outside this file.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header comment and imports
sections.what: Explains the two-level citation model, and brings in the data-fetching tool and the citation drawer.
sections.why: The comment records the design. The imports supply the tools the hook needs.
sections.watch_out: The comment describes the design, so keep it accurate if the fetch changes.

sections.name: FullCitationTarget
sections.title: Target shape
sections.what: Defines what a caller passes to open a citation: the project, the field path, an optional specific quote id and which tab to start on.
sections.why: Lets a caller ask for one exact quote, not just the first one listed.
sections.watch_out: Field paths can hold several comma-separated paths, which the endpoint must accept.

sections.name: EvidenceResponse, isResearchId
sections.title: Response shape and research id check
sections.what: Defines the shape of the evidence response and provides a check that an id belongs to a registered research source, which starts with rs-.
sections.why: Research sources are fetched by id, and the prefix is how the code tells them apart from project fields.
sections.watch_out: The check depends on the rs- prefix, so changing how ids are made breaks routing.

sections.name: useFullCitation (part 1)
sections.title: Address choice, fetch and Escape key
sections.what: Holds the target and open state, and a direct citation for non-project sources. Picks the fetch address: a research source by id, or a project field by project and path. Fetches only while the drawer is open and no direct citation is given. Opening and closing functions set the state. The Escape key is captured first so pages underneath do not also react.
sections.why: Likely reason: fetching only while open avoids needless requests. The Escape capture is explained in the code: other handlers should not fire while the drawer is open.
sections.watch_out: While the drawer is open, no other handler sees Escape.

sections.name: useFullCitation (part 2)
sections.title: Citation build and error messages
sections.what: Turns the fetched response into one citation, choosing the clicked quote when an id is given. Shows the right message when the fetch fails, the quote is no longer active, or no quote is linked. Passes the result to the citation drawer.
sections.why: Stated in the code: a failed fetch must not look like a full quote, and a missing link must be reported as a linkage gap, not a finding.
sections.watch_out: The message wording is deliberate. Change it only with care, since it tells readers what the gap means.

summary: A shared helper that opens the full source citation for a value, fetches the complete quote when needed, and reports loading and errors honestly.
purpose: When a user opens a full citation or a source, shows the complete verbatim quote, publisher, date and link for that value.
why: The header explains that list screens carry only short quotes, so full text is fetched on demand. Errors are shown rather than hidden, so a short quote never looks like the full one.
how: Holds the target and open state. Picks an address: a research source fetched by id, or a project field fetched by project and field path. Fetches only while the drawer is open. Turns the response into one citation and a quote list, picks the clicked quote, and works out the right message when a quote is missing, unlinked or the fetch fails. Closes on Escape before other key handlers see it.
inputs: A target with project id, project name, field path, optional evidence id and optional starting tab. Or a ready citation for a non-project source.
outputs: A citation drawer, error or loading text, and functions to open a citation or close it.
risks: The fetch call sets no query function in this file, so it depends on a default fetcher configured elsewhere. The project id is placed in the address without encoding. While the drawer is open, the Escape key is captured, so other parts of the page never see it.
debug: If a citation shows no quote, check the field path and whether evidence exists for that field. If the message says the citation could not load, check the request to the evidence endpoint in the browser tools. If Escape does nothing, check for another open dialog.
